turns.user: I'd rather not say my exact age.
turns.message:
That's fine — you can sort out eligibility directly with the provider. Here are the four services that cover San Ramon City Hall to San Ramon Regional Medical Center on Wednesday, August 12. Each will need to confirm you qualify when you call:

- **Senior Express Van (San Ramon)** — (925) 938-7433. $5 each way, door-to-door, seniors 55+, no proof required. Book at least a day ahead. Runs weekdays 8:30 AM–1:00 PM, so 10:00 AM works.
- **LINK Paratransit** — (925) 938-7433. $5 each way, cash, door-to-door. For riders 18+ with a disability; requires a County Connection LINK ADA application. Book 1–7 days ahead. 10:00 AM is within their hours.
- **One-Seat Regional Ride** — (925) 680-2134. $3, door-to-door, for riders 18+ with a disability. Book 1–3 days ahead. Their operating hours aren't on file, so ask whether 10:00 AM works.
- **Mobility Matters** — (925) 284-6161. Free volunteer drivers, for seniors 60+ or veterans who live in Contra Costa County. Needs 7 days' notice and is meant as a last resort. Hours aren't on file — confirm the time when you call.

Of these, Senior Express Van is the simplest starting point since it asks for no proof and the time is confirmed available.

There's also public transit: walk about 4 minutes to Bollinger Canyon Rd & Alcosta Blvd, take the Dublin/Pleasanton BART–San Ramon bus at 10:03 AM, then a 14-minute walk from Camino Ramon & Norris Canyon Rd — arriving around 10:31 AM.

OPTIMAT can't book for you, so call whichever you prefer — and note the notice requirements, especially Mobility Matters' 7 days.

turns.message:
**Mobility Matters is your one option for that Sunday 5:00 AM ride** — but you'll need to book it well ahead.

- **Mobility Matters** (volunteer drivers, door-to-door, free): call **(925) 284-6161**. You qualify as a Contra Costa resident 60+. - **Senior Express Van (San Ramon)** also serves this route, but weekdays only, 8:30 AM–1:00 PM.

One-Seat Regional Ride is out — it requires a disability certification.

There's also a public transit path, but it's essentially a 27-minute walk of about a mile, which probably isn't what you want at 5 AM.

results.title: General accessibility question, not a trip request

turns.user: Does BART have wheelchair access at every station?
turns.message:
Yes — every BART station has wheelchair access. All stations have elevators, wider fare gates near the elevators, and BART trains have level boarding with designated wheelchair areas.

Two practical notes: at some stations you'll need to take two elevators to get from street level to the platform, and if an elevator is out of service, the station agent (there's a courtesy phone by the elevator entrance) will help you get in or out.

If you'd like, I can also look for door-to-door ride options for a specific trip — just tell me where you're starting from and where you're headed.

data.query: Does BART have wheelchair accessible access at every station? Are all BART stations accessible with elevators?
data.answer: All BART stations have accessible elevators and wheelchair access at every station. BART trains feature level boarding. Paratransit service is available for those unable to use BART trains.
